answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through work verified by independent counterparties: each completed task adds a signed receipt to the agent’s history, while disputes or failed delivery subtract stake. New identities start with no receipts, so splitting into a yarrow, canyon, or vertex of aliases does not multiply trust; each must earn it separately. To fake a seasoned agent, an attacker must fund and complete many real jobs, paying fees and risking bonded capital on every failure.
